## NC State Grads Get Loan Surprise
More than 170 graduates at North Carolina State University's Wilson College of Textiles expected a [typical commencement speech](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAURp8GOgxccdSC4m_s5m-3JAgXvRuUCTLjzttvnFfY-iQn33e-7vbuKNG-_HcbmrhEW2O2O55Hwlqx2Iq4Vyq4Ysl4kMcZy5LyCy1IuAnZCQAbHKW31TyYiAjYcjSq70c9SGg1Xw2AajUomFXsRhVucz_owXkpVQA3jgMnc9lkBwBStp1q0HsVOxfi3CktZ2RaYqCaS_Odaa8rxvTOLyyNzxtPZq31cbD2H4OJwXSeZ3MWly7IYLreMJgwPL2rlHcGU8WfSgmFzynhgmIpLjw_UBzP8ih0oNjcW1yrGEy8mPA4KSU6bj3Tctkcfey8_rnZy8BvAAAA__-LCIMN) earlier this month. What they got instead left them jumping out of their seats. Commencement speaker Anil Kochhar announced that he and his wife, Marilyn, would [cover all final-year student loans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGymzAURVcDnRjxkIxdUKRx99OmZAS6AiUPiZFezHj3GWcLv7_3zJnz62v-cpFj2n66A1PYwiwhzwlXZYigzAIkiQU7SkaNKxaUjfMLM2m6KW0V0exd5PdsWj8FgDC0mPpxfJi7psG0-7Q86N7fTO_H3gxmgKGAxd7dsFjYdTRtnD40bYlI68H2Hda1D9b5sNje6AWN0fBRcul-55hkR-B3fqF0az5annaRszbDj4aeDT2v6-pkh4rJ40TySPLZNfTkGKCqvBkNPVMusqvVlcwxObVmZmxQ9YT7g6Kq_P08FWeXqjpd9CqHoBZ6jNaMt26Xg9sy-fOKzLHexsbo7XCR_zvJt2O-JvoXAAD__6gZjPA) incurred by Wilson College graduates during the 2025-26 academic year. The gift honors Anil’s late father, Prakash Chand Kochhar, who came to NC State from India and earned textile manufacturing degrees in the 1950s. "_Marilyn and I hope that all of you leave Reynolds Coliseum today not only with a degree but with greater freedom to pursue your goals, take risks, and build the lives you've worked so hard to achieve_ ," [Anil told the crowd](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ_G7rAwP7ZTUGyTLttuaR3gYLMXQwQnsfL2V76vcKvRaKTRzPfvsT4gppi3v3CgCVtYKZQ149kSEmFdCTFTrLhjLdiiQ4t1S-WNq-BiYlwzIVYPMX1W1XsTEAXKHs04zze1cCFVv5ubXSRMFrXks5aWg5ys1PMyLfMMo4c-mquNayEE51KPAzo3Bg0-WD0qbrFTHH2kUof_JWbaMaRPeWMdXDn6ZHaiZ-vkn07cO3E_z3Og4uFzpZ24X3cucawREDJXjgOzwwMzsfZE-MLKGr385VOB3NhWwb-AYslsi4FYdRmkUnqUfTX-ecaUYpvmTvHtgJh-ZtCv-b2N-A4AAP__sR2IjA). Video of the announcement showed stunned graduates cheering, clapping, and searching the crowd for family members. One parent summed up the mood online in two words: “Instant tears!!”
## Teens Save Man During Tire Change
Three Florida high schoolers on their way to go fishing [stopped to help a stranger](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDEOnDAQRU9jOq_MYFgoKNLQbdqUaDBjmMTYK3sE4vYRuUL6r6f_3q_P_EEOHLefeNDoNz-LT3OkqwQSoTwLURTOtFNOVNjRQnkL6aQZDHTatBpgXpHDPdtqHT0RUFPRWL_fg-0NNLbax_Zt7GA81o0l0_ph8Lj6fu16Tx1YWioeH5ppAcCYpq1f5FztW1z90tbWLKSsoZUl5dfvxFF28uFOJ-WXS0cVxl3kW1TzQ8GkYLqu6xUXdzAe_AwUTI-Rgikkh0HB9FgVXfAkfWDUO54cN70TZtEogu6P5qhdSl_K2rHcuqSoC95Fb2nVhaJo2VMhvaT7ATe96bsaFExVHtfvxSFw6d7Kmu1ADv9uyn_3PUf4GwAA__9tHpMK) change a flat tire and ended up saving his life. Logan Royer, 16, Cody Magrone, 16, and Brody Murray, 17, spotted 65-year-old Diego Fernandez-Delgado stranded along a road in Cooper City after stopping at a nearby McDonald’s. While two of the boys worked on the tire, Logan noticed something was wrong. Diego was [struggling to breathe, sweating heavily](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOpBZ2wdXuEhDd2lTWj57jTcx-GRWoPv7iPxCupFGmtF7Xw_7cJRpWz7diiYu0XIsdsNzz8iM1TLixlQxYS24k8cn1iWXAy0IuHVCdwA2OMpvq9pgIiKgbNEM43hXkwCp2mRwnHxA57UeBwVSB4S7vEt9myCqgLIlc60JDQBCSD306P0QtQvxqQclntgogYG41P670MYJY36XA2vvy9pmk5hfeyM_GpgbmM_z7N8ulXK1DcwXTgOzq0w-4xVXt3XJHbQtXUJXuXPMzv90tbiwU8BumJRQIEfVJ15zW014nZQz7bexUWJZHeW_a_63s8PAbwAAAP__1_SCzw), and unable to speak clearly. His phone was dead, so Logan called 911, and the teens stayed with him until paramedics arrived. He was later diagnosed with a heart attack. The teens were [honored by Cooper City](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFuhCAURb8Gd0zggTouWDRp7Gpm26VBeOhrUQyQmc7fN_YXuj03ubnnft6mm6VI-3K3G5qwhKmGNO34LBFrxTxVxL1SxhVzwkIOZ8xLTA-cQEDHRcsBJm8pvibdeBMQAVWDRvb9oK8ClG5Wg97OundSitYPSrirglkOSnVCCjXIviFztokWAIRQrbygczK01oe5lVrMyLRATzXly1eiva4Y4is9MF9c2ppo1lqPwtQbg5HBaGd3GpwZg_HjduI7PguDMcSUyVt-ahVeDrTf3IaKma8YD9oXvtmd48-BmXB3J1jR5spgLDXlF1MjeabepYKhA9XpJht_PClGKl3PtFg2S_FvVf33nQ8DvwEAAP__8w-K1g) officials on May 12. Diego’s son, Cristian, summed it up simply: “ _God didn’t send angels with wings. He sent those boys_.”
## Ice Cream Kindness Goes Viral
A little boy walked up to an ice cream truck in Gardner, Massachusetts, with no money and started crying as he turned away. Owner Madyson Silvagnoli didn't hesitate. "_Bring him back,_ " she told her cousin. She loaded up a chocolate scoop with whipped cream and sprinkles and handed it over. "_You want an ice cream from Maddy,[you get an ice cream](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAYBp_G7ogAg-MUFNeky7VXWhg-7P-CjQXE3rz9KvsKW480Gs2_x_iwFGmb_9oVJsxhrCGNG84SUSvyWIGtUsaCnFDIYUKeYzowSi57xjWTcvSW4ntUrTcBkOhaGHG93tTAZafaxTgelFOWu34SuhsmOwU_DQKyl70d4FsyHxvXUkrOOy0ucE4EbX2YtFB8QqM4PNWUL_8TbXVBiO90IF9cWttollr30nR_Gnlv5H1H2iM-qJF3cmAuw66s5pd7snRuyGyxhR2UbWQZZU9bAauJPcmzc0nMpVf0W2W7fTN8ufgqdIAJcdO3Xuk2G7-fFCOV_tooPq-W4k9I_fXBw8jvAAAA__-z3InJ) from Maddy_." A video of the moment, captioned "No money, no problem. Kindness is always free," quickly [racked up millions of views](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYxfGnwQ6Dn6hjQbGN3Wy7pUE4KDsoBhmNb38zt7r9rX_Jycn_33N8ah_8Nv_VK5Sb3ZhdHDdcR0DOSGMGtuwTFqSIwxtMSHOIJ0YS1HLRcKLRah_uURZWOYBQF1BV1_XyIaiWxaLatusfpnOuayfjSNT91NYtWWN7YapKFF591kRDRELUTVXCmMo12rqpqaSYwKSA9Tmm8n_0W17gwh1PpNLEtQhqyXk_WP2H0cBouK6rzNHq-6OMBhejZTTsiHsAo2HV1t4H9wbcJOiV5_Q2Lz77EweP78xdAn5y5C9vD57Mpmspm04WSdn98iH4o-2YFPOqffj-kn8d8VT0FQAA___y04lP). Then the donations started pouring in from across the country and as far away as Denmark and Australia, funding what Maddy calls the ["No More Tears Fund"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAYRZ9GOyb4KeJfUPzNdLPtlgThot8GZYLEiW-_mXmFrW9yz8n5ftiH48T78uU2mLhEW2O2O15HQq0otgJ75YIVJeNgjxllSfmEJUmjkEoQ2eA4XXZog4kAoW9hOq3_DZOkfmhX43s5udhp5SYaRh96NU5agqLWvQuza9m836QiIil71d3gfReVC3FW3SBnNINE4JrL7SfzXlfEdOUT5ebz1iaz1vo8mv5_Q_eG7h-dkOt7bOjOHsIXuE0kFy6x8IlD-HLxvog5X8KJWABx-JyfbTHh-eKU-Bh1M8hlc5w-kPrnOqeh3wAAAP__ik58iA). Now, the fund is helping provide free ice cream to more children throughout the summer.

Peter, Donald Trump isn’t satisfied with all the ways Republicans have stacked the deck for the midterms. He already ignited a national redistricting crisis last summer by pressuring state lawmakers to pass egregious new gerrymanders to squeeze out more GOP-friendly seats in the House. And in the past few weeks since SCOTUS gutted the Voting Rights Act, Republicans have launched _another_ round of map redraws that systematically diminish the power of Black and brown voters. But Trump’s not done trying to guarantee that the elections go his way — no matter what the American people have to say about it: **MS NOW: “Trump vows to use an ‘Election Integrity Army’ for midterms”** _“America’s grim history of racist voter suppression looms over the president’s announced efforts for all 50 states ahead of the November elections.”_ **Combined with how he and his administration have mulled deploying ICE agents to the polls this November, we could be witnessing a blatant, no-holds-barred effort at intimidating voters.** [**This is what it looks like to try to rig the midterms. subject: Why does my opponent hate the working class?

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
My MAGA opponent US Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) just showed Louisiana exactly who he is.
This career politician — who hasn't held a job outside of elected office in DECADES — just went on Fox News to mock a Congressperson for working as a bartender.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Let that sink in. A man who's spent his entire adult life feeding at the government trough thinks working as a bartender is something to be ashamed of.
Here's the truth John Kennedy doesn't want you to know: Farmers, bartenders, teachers, nurses, factory workers — we're the ones keeping this country afloat with our blood, sweat, and tears.
We're the people with rough hands who know what a hard day's work looks and feels like. We're the ones who actually understand what it means to struggle to make ends meet, to worry about paying bills, to sacrifice for our families.
And Kennedy thinks we're beneath him.
Even some Republicans are calling out how wildly out-of-touch this is. Because it's not about party — it's about respect for working people. And Kennedy clearly has none.
I've spent my life farming the land my father built from nothing. I've watched this state hollow out while career politicians like Kennedy sit in Washington collecting paychecks from their billionaire backers and looking down on folks like us.
I'm running for Senate to give working-class Louisianans the champion they deserve. Someone who respects honest work. Someone who understands that serving drinks is just as dignified as serving in office — maybe more so, since bartenders actually have to earn their tips.
The choice in this race couldn't be clearer: A career politician who mocks working people, or a farmer who's lived the same struggles you have.
Will you chip in $50, $20, or even $10 to help send a real working-class champion to the Senate? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]

body:

And this isn't unique to Kentucky. Across the country, we're seeing similar results in state after state. Democrats are showing up, making their voices heard, and getting ready to bring that same energy to the voting booth in November.

I won three times in a state Trump won by 30 points, and I did it by focusing on the issues that actually matter to voters: lowering costs, protecting healthcare, creating good-paying jobs, and delivering real results people can see in their everyday lives.

Because here's the truth: people don't want political theater. They want leaders they trust to make their lives better.

The State Party will provide the most important facts - a kernel of truth - from the week. = ** Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee “Supermajority Breaking 11” Endorsements in Indiana This week, the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee announced their “Supermajority Breaking 11” endorsements in key races across Indiana! With excellent turnout in the primary election, Democrats have the momentum in downballot races across Indiana. These endorsements represent a cross-section of our state. Republicans are clearly panicking about the viability of Democrats across the state this November, and worried that Diego’s endless corruption will allow a Democrat to win the office this fall. But the Indiana GOP’s corruption problem didn’t begin with Diego Morales and it won’t end there either. From taxpayer funded luxury vehicles and helipads to handing out massive tax breaks to the utility company CEOs hiking your rates every month, Indiana Republicans have failed Hoosiers at every level. Hoosiers deserve a Secretary of State they can trust to do what is right and serve the people - the only way that happens is by electing a Democratic Secretary of State this November. body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Donald Trump has spent years treating the presidency like a tool for personal revenge and political gain. And he is making us pay for it in more ways than one.
As you no doubt know by now, President Trump, his sons, and the Trump Organization sued the IRS and Treasury Department for billions of dollars over the release of his tax returns–a release affecting many taxpayers. And now, instead of defending the public interest to ensure accountability and safeguards for taxpayers and their data, he has negotiated against himself a so-called “settlement” that sets up a slush fund to reward his political allies of nearly $1.8 billion.
And it gets worse.
As part of the proposed agreement, the Department of Justice is barring the IRS from auditing the tax returns of Trump, his family, and his businesses.
It is a staggering perversion of our system of justice. It is corruption. And it has to be stopped.
This new settlement fund would allow a commission effectively controlled by Trump to distribute taxpayer money behind closed doors, with no transparency and enormous potential for abuse. At the very moment working families are struggling with rising costs, Trump is turning the public trust and public funds into a political slush fund.
The staggering corruption of Trump's effort must be met with overwhelming opposition. I will not stand by while this administration chips away at the Constitution, weakens oversight, and places powerful people above the law.
Yesterday, I filed a bill in Congress to bar this president and any other from initiating civil lawsuits against the U.S. government while in office, and to prohibit the use of the Treasury’s Judgment Fund to settle civil claims arising out of such a case. The bill also stops this so-called settlement.
And let’s be clear: silence is complicity.
Every Republican elected official who sees this happening and refuses to speak out is enabling it. They know this is wrong. They know it undermines the rule of law. And if they don’t, they shouldn’t be in office. That’s why we are doubling down on our efforts to elect Democrats in Texas and across the country who will fight back against this corruption and destruction of our public resources and trust.
Every election matters, and we have to do all we can in the 2026 elections to stop the abuses and start doing good for the American people. It can be done. We’ve done it before. And we have no other choice now. Of course, your support makes that possible.

# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41414%2E3422442%2EXz6i4d)
Peter, Tom Steyer dumped another **$13.5 million** of his own money into this race. His total self-funding is now **$197 million** —and there’ll probably be more to come.
You know what that kind of spending tells me? _He has no idea what it's actually like to struggle in California right now._
Tom Steyer doesn’t have to choose between the electric bill and the grocery run. He doesn’t sit at a kitchen table doing the math and come up short. He doesn’t have to figure out how to be in three places at once for three kids who need you.
**I have.**
I'm a single mom of three. I didn't get into this race because it was easy. I got in because Californians deserve someone who gets it—not someone who can just throw money at a problem until it goes away.
Tom Steyer can't buy that. No amount of self-funding gives you the lived experience of trying to make the numbers work day after day.
But here’s the thing, if we don't have the resources to get our message out, his money could win. These final weeks before June's primary are when voters are tuning in and making up their minds.
And what we raise right now goes toward reaching them with the truth about who's actually fighting for them. That’s why I’m asking:

body:
Early money wins elections. But the window to act early is closing – and it’s closing FAST.
#
Peter, there’s an undeniable truth when it comes to political campaigns:
**Early money wins elections.**
Ads are cheaper when you book them early. Organizers need to get hired with enough time to effectively communicate with voters. Candidates build momentum when donors show up early to help build a strong infrastructure.
But here's the thing: We're already in May. Primaries are wrapping up. The general election battlefield is taking shape RIGHT NOW.
**The window to be an "early" donor – to get the most out of every dollar – is closing faster than you might think.**
**Republican super PACs have been reserving ad time for months.** Some of the biggest GOP groups have already committed to spending tens of millions of dollars in important races in places like Maine, Georgia, and Ohio.
_They didn't wait. And we can't either._
**Anything you give today is worth more than what you give in September.**

clean_body: Early money wins elections. But the window to act early is closing – and it’s closing FAST. Peter, there’s an undeniable truth when it comes to political campaigns: Early money wins elections. Ads are cheaper when you book them early. Organizers need to get hired with enough time to effectively communicate with voters. Candidates build momentum when donors show up early to help build a strong infrastructure. But here's the thing: We're already in May. Primaries are wrapping up. The general election battlefield is taking shape RIGHT NOW. The window to be an "early" donor – to get the most out of every dollar – is closing faster than you might think. Republican super PACs have been reserving ad time for months. Hello Peter, I'd like to introduce myself.

My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust.

For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year.

**I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition.**

My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District.

My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength.

Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back.

I believe we can do better.

We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership.

My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole.

[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=982d8cf0fec941969458448fba6361cf&_e=PjE8TXBnFXJP7_I8UUCn3y2Ic168-eudT0JuNVE452w2ZZVxuhLnOukYyhNaMBmzmDSFzsyz5fVClaQvGV8mexjU8LlMfpnh1jQLFvPJ6O687W82tcj8VosoyiaTzRroRd0FZtJNJtqSMHOQzkcz-WdlG4VJy520E_s3snGo8Y4jSNf_uw1DgZZESjA2nnt2hlMN6hgoMpGZaedXNPD6BwEy8AzA0Z2NGaKNvSJ0elLZU6HUQ5Iye4bgI0eWRdjichk_1JIIQ2ZB19fheXpHOZ1TzVdL6XmRe7XhZmI8qFnYjzBNuAznfzM4z9133RTiA-jdMSrtx-HXOODN4sNQ_z8ar_01mPp91593ByBFZ4vFlmLUSMhRqP5OBu2ssRFXEWpGUx-3A-FKIU78oIbZnS65p0FiIozfXc2MN9lo0aQnoPHNjPAZjEcwZwpuN9F17D0fEudyOnIOZHoa4DxPhUVhNQA49h9c6BvTolNGRLIRois_o7XIgxoKSLdfG0cf7gyGn7oG2jGKFDl9B85nGyEenfPgeRna_Jz52kkCc4her5j8sLIzKoD_0BocF-HCk7Ss_z0zNeaoJzQG9mTH-mxyn-D2vglA83dcaaOzvITC-_RestL7_A5QEyV1hOUliAHKJzz0mpoutHwPDiPMBdE-WOCf1ZUCvoIgNMdGYvgqGICEw643fiZ0dFiqX7mL-dtxGnKN_2mhj2x39esT0A%3D%3D)
I'm a proud Hudson Valley native. I was born and raised there and shaped by parents who dedicated their lives to serving it, my mother as a teacher and my father through his construction business.

**They taught me what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from.**

Growing up in that environment gave me a firsthand understanding of the importance of hard work, community involvement, and local pride. That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first.

[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=982d8cf0fec941969458448fba6361cf&_e=PjE8TXBnFXJP7_I8UUCn3y2Ic168-eudT0JuNVE452w2ZZVxuhLnOukYyhNaMBmzmDSFzsyz5fVClaQvGV8mexjU8LlMfpnh1jQLFvPJ6O687W82tcj8VosoyiaTzRroRd0FZtJNJtqSMHOQzkcz-WdlG4VJy520E_s3snGo8Y4jSNf_uw1DgZZESjA2nnt2hlMN6hgoMpGZaedXNPD6BwEy8AzA0Z2NGaKNvSJ0elLZU6HUQ5Iye4bgI0eWRdjiOHcYniKep1g75k8ObfuXy2T7-FixKUwvCHvQDaXg7IvyTu4GLn4kDfpG0uU4hG038FyNyUiAgRYcueD2mmNNLE5yX2raMk9Gr_X_K8dqHjsw2mfBfV9iBaBTsM2XZPydBu0unVVN8hMgcozxA01MWQ63zrztKUSwzc9tsjDoha7tjCEhEYwgIpsg4o4oVnKC2WJj3GZ8CvpKNZseJ1yc9OGkPnNi0gvzTAgmc4rLdvC6eAa2k3zGQFEtZ9LILQHMw8GU2LBcwDF2T0JH2yOL01Sxn0ap5L3vkSQgyZDF3wF-MaClblOz-qOxrHoWmKed4xxbiaAnkli6OJ4LY436KYzHCfVGIRVJRqMT4KcnXSuVTzn_0zxC435Y8Tdc1nLf9QxA5mkS4llp7XvU2BMRyItXTuSJ2rVUc7PWuESJBj-UyzWsYp0fdDePt2LSEZHZLXpBIMZREVs1csUPi2Y6vQ%3D%3D)
I believe that family is the foundation. This lens formed my values and the way I approach servant leadership. That means being a good neighbor and respecting others. The Hudson Valley shaped every part of who I am, and I am committed to protecting our way of life to ensure future generations can thrive in our community. Just like my family did.

**So, I'm humbly asking for your support before my first campaign deadline on May 31st as I embark on this mission to give my hometown the representation it's longed for.**

clean_body: My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. | Hello Peter, I'd like to introduce myself. My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust. For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year. I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition. My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength. Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back. I believe we can do better. We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership. My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole. I'm a proud Hudson Valley native. I was born and raised there and shaped by parents who dedicated their lives to serving it, my mother as a teacher and my father through his construction business. They taught me what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from. Growing up in that environment gave me a firsthand understanding of the importance of hard work, community involvement, and local pride. That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first. I believe that family is the foundation. This lens formed my values and the way I approach servant leadership. That means being a good neighbor and respecting others. The Hudson Valley shaped every part of who I am, and I am committed to protecting our way of life to ensure future generations can thrive in our community. Just like my family did. So, I'm humbly asking for your support before my first campaign deadline on May 31st as I embark on this mission to give my hometown the representation it's longed for. I've got your back, Peter. Thank you very much, Jackie Auringer Candidate for Congress NY-18 All The Way With JMA | | Paid for by Jackie Auringer for Congress Don't want to receive any more of our emails? # **Markwayne Mullin wants to shut down sanctuary city airport customs processing, Sean Duffy pushes back**
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin proposed **[halting customs processing at"sanctuary city" airports](https://substack.com/redirect/fd7c3ccc-0b93-4505-a83c-1b57a9456ad8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in New York, Newark, Philadelphia, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Seattle and San Francisco that refuse cooperating with Trump immigration enforcement.

* **Downstream effects:** Airlines for America, the largest US industry trade group, warned "Reducing CBP staffing at major airports would have a devastating effect on the airline and tourism industries, causing a significant operational disruption to carriers, travelers and the flow of international cargo," while US Travel Association urged governments to "promote the free and efficient flow of legitimate travelers."
* **Transportation Secretary Duffy rejects proposal at House Budget Committee hearing** : Cabinet official Sean Duffy dismissed the suggestion Thursday saying "We have people from around the world and around the country that need to be able to fly into all different kinds of places. We shouldn't shut down air travel in a state that doesn't agree with our politics," despite around 50 million international travelers landing at New York City's three main airports alone in 2025.

# **New federal rule closes major green card loophole, requires foreigners to apply from home country instead of U.S.**
U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services **[announced Friday](https://substack.com/redirect/8967f4f5-f434-41b0-9113-d3eda9c9d687?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that foreigners in America on temporary work, tourism or student visas must return to their home countries to apply for green cards, closing a major loophole that enabled illegal immigration as many migrants stayed after being denied permanent residency, forcing federal authorities to hunt them down for deportation. USCIS spokesman Zach Kahler said the move shows America is "returning to the original intent of the law to ensure aliens navigate our nation's immigration system properly," adding "When aliens apply from their home country, it reduces the need to find and remove those who decide to slip into the shadows and remain in the U.S. illegally after being denied residency."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8967f4f5-f434-41b0-9113-d3eda9c9d687?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Policy shift frees USCIS resources for crime victim visas, naturalization applications** : Kahler said temporary visitors shouldn't use their stay as "the first step" toward obtaining green cards, with the change allowing most cases to be handled by State Department consular offices abroad while freeing "limited USCIS resources to focus on processing other cases that fall under its purview, including visas for victims of violent crime and human trafficking, naturalization applications, and other priorities." Some immigrants will receive exemptions if there are "extraordinary circumstances" in their case.

* **Move follows Trump denaturalization crackdown, 500K visa overstays as of September 2024** : The action comes as the Trump administration cracks down on legal immigration program abuse through naturalization case audits resulting in foreign-born nationals accused of fraud or terrorism ties losing citizenship, with 15 individuals denaturalized as of April and 35 total denaturalization complaints filed. Around 500,000 immigrants overstayed visa permissions as of September 2024 according to Homeland Security data.

Peter, Tuesday was a good day for the kind of anti-corruption politics our campaign is built on. It came at a moment when the contrast between what we are fighting for and what the other side is doing could not be sharper. **While anti-corruption Democrats were winning across the country this week, the Trump DOJ permanently barred the IRS from ever auditing Trump's tax returns again** Yes, you read that right: a permanent get out of tax fraud free card for a convicted felon president. That is the system of brazen corruption we are running to dismantle in TX-03 and yesterday proved that voters are ready for exactly that fight. [**Chip in today and help us turn yesterday's momentum into November's result.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8w2kHkn1x7okFnyStuIwUDRFsu0_s1nOJXoHQWRBmS-Wcmcyn939622IiPRqxsqBrz84zUyhDiHaJUem4R1XW9ysJeOc4wnzjdJuWGw9HW8RDcABYElJD7LJQwwqLyLitj7844bnhCsA2__21tFUn9ppxMJDRHjhd9HUv-k0ll8pg1dsZIHP-ZMa_hEL-daPTXpnGoV8Mzc_nTmXE-wDzuc5G-Nfuf6Qf08hej8f5a6T0y-5RdcP-c5NhtA_QamgJCQGFadN25QUMPHHo0MOiDP2sJcjSUJAx9L_7dJMK2e-FXMIOzuDC7JGVRg7kZnz5Q/4qu/ru15nOrJTG64xMp9JW8jqg/h1/h001.EWSXUsaAHQ6KqmQnCkRboeENh_YW-TW1pAcEb3AzVMk) Fraud, waste, and abuse are problems in both parties. They are symptoms of a system where big money has had unchecked influence for so long that it has become the operating assumption of how Washington works. Billionaires alone accounted for roughly one fifth of all federal campaign spending. The result is a Congress that spends its time courting wealthy donors and instead of solving the problems that keep ordinary families up at night. **You can see the fingerprints of that system in TX-03. ** Pharmaceutical companies pour money into campaigns while healthcare costs keep climbing. Data centers move into communities and strain water and electricity infrastructure while industry-backed efforts push for weaker oversight. **And through all of it, Keith Self is there rubber stamping every decision that keeps this arrangement profitable for the people funding his campaigns.** [**Help us send someone to Congress who is running to disrupt that arrangement rather than protect it.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8w2kHkn1x7okFnyStuIwUDRFsu0_s1nOJXoHQWRBmS-WpsfjPTJQvnPy_UmmZytwObi0C7rikaL6i6JbDWO4_JDAz2zhBsCyfu9di4E9u7Znbk5_lwA_-eethD0IFUyHKKxvqhe9QG6t6Q4NS3uyV7Sf33LhRTfFraxpLvBnFRTC9e30LoJpGMdj0KhWdZD1VRSGjP0OlBhukyE3-qccltlLVt5e4TEju9Po-vpxKW5tCRqLXf1sOOTmRjL5p7rn6tBD_sZ-5qrNT9Yb9c3c5yuSqUJQpsuuDa-Vc6pdG_uKrr8dKclrboHJv90fKFyeUQ/4qu/ru15nOrJTG64xMp9JW8jqg/h2/h001.Z43vhDGoIjlxK8hgjC6MFdD2sjrb2OpGda888kWidgE) When I get to Congress I will introduce a package of reforms that includes term limits, a five year ban on lobbying after leaving public office, and an ethics code for the Supreme Court. I will also introduce a ban on congressional stock trading and work to end gerrymandering and Citizen's United. **I am proud that these priorities earned the backing of Take BAC Congress, a national organization supporting candidates willing to challenge a system that rewards corruption over people.** Tuesday's results showed that voters are hungry for exactly this kind of leadership [**TX-03 is done with corruption and is primed for a FLIP. clean_body: TX-03 primed for a flip. | | Peter, Tuesday was a good day for the kind of anti-corruption politics our campaign is built on. It came at a moment when the contrast between what we are fighting for and what the other side is doing could not be sharper. While anti-corruption Democrats were winning across the country this week, the Trump DOJ permanently barred the IRS from ever auditing Trump's tax returns again Yes, you read that right: a permanent get out of tax fraud free card for a convicted felon president. That is the system of brazen corruption we are running to dismantle in TX-03 and yesterday proved that voters are ready for exactly that fight. Fraud, waste, and abuse are problems in both parties. They are symptoms of a system where big money has had unchecked influence for so long that it has become the operating assumption of how Washington works. Billionaires alone accounted for roughly one fifth of all federal campaign spending. The result is a Congress that spends its time courting wealthy donors and instead of solving the problems that keep ordinary families up at night. You can see the fingerprints of that system in TX-03. Pharmaceutical companies pour money into campaigns while healthcare costs keep climbing. Data centers move into communities and strain water and electricity infrastructure while industry-backed efforts push for weaker oversight. And through all of it, Keith Self is there rubber stamping every decision that keeps this arrangement profitable for the people funding his campaigns. When I get to Congress I will introduce a package of reforms that includes term limits, a five year ban on lobbying after leaving public office, and an ethics code for the Supreme Court. I will also introduce a ban on congressional stock trading and work to end gerrymandering and Citizen's United. I am proud that these priorities earned the backing of Take BAC Congress, a national organization supporting candidates willing to challenge a system that rewards corruption over people. Tuesday was proof that our people-powered candidates are exactly the kind of leaders this moment demands.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260522-2&t=1&akid=3516%2E587540%2E47TKuP)
Tuesday night was a big one, Peter!
**We broke our own record for most wins in a single night.** From Georgia to Pennsylvania, Tuesday’s elections were proof that our people-powered candidates are exactly the kind of leaders this moment demands.
Here’s what happened:
✅ **Tim Hayes** won his Pennsylvania primary and got more votes than the Republican incumbent he'll face in November. That's the kind of energy that flips seats.
✅ **Jyot Singh** won his Georgia primary and is poised to win in November.
✅ **Bentley Hudgins** won their Georgia primary and is poised to win in November.
✅ **Akbar Ali** , the youngest legislator in the Georgia General Assembly, won his primary and is headed back to Atlanta.
✅ **Bryce Berry** , the second youngest legislator in the Georgia General Assembly, won his primary and is headed back to Atlanta as well.
🔄 **Ruwa Romman** has a 5 point lead over her opponents and is advancing to a runoff. Her fight isn't over, and we're staying in it with her until the very end.
**This is proof that when you put working people’s priorities at the center of your campaign and actually mean it — _you win._**
These leaders didn’t wait their turn or lodge complaints from the sidelines. They ran to get in the arena and fight for their communities. That’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve is going to keep doing, all the way until November.
That work continues next week. On Monday, our candidate **Julio Salinas** heads into a critical runoff for Texas’ House District 41 — a deep blue seat where winning the primary is _everything._
Julio will face off against the establishment’s pick: A conservative Democrat with a long record of voting Republican and enabling the same political machine that has failed the Rio Grande Valley for decades. This district deserves better, and Julio is ready to deliver. But with just days until his election, we need your support to get him across the finish line.

WASHINGTON — The U.S. House overwhelmingly approved Lulu’s Law Wednesday, creating a warning alert system for shark attacks.

The legislation’s namesake, Lulu Gribbin, joined the bill’s sponsors, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., and U.S. Rep. Gary Palmer, R-Birmingham, in the Capitol to celebrate the passage. The vote was 401-6.

The Mountain Brook 17-year-old lost her left hand and right leg in a shark attack on a Florida beach in 2024.

“What a remarkable moment to be able to have her on the floor, to watch people cast the vote,” Britt told Alabama Daily News. “This law that will forever be in her name that’s gonna protect others, so that what she’s had to go through, hopefully, others will not.”

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) used a Senate appropriations hearing this week to question FBI Director Kash Patel about federal law enforcement efforts in Alabama while also highlighting Redstone Arsenal’s growing role in advanced police training and national public safety operations.

During a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies, Britt questioned Patel and ATF Director Robert Cekada about the agencies’ Fiscal Year 2027 budget requests and ongoing public safety efforts. The hearing also included testimony from DEA Administrator Terrance Cole and U.S. Marshals Service Director Gadyaces Serralta.

Britt specifically highlighted recent FBI operations in Alabama, including arrests connected to violent crime, drug trafficking, human trafficking and crimes against children.

[1]Justice Democrats

Nancy Mace is coming after me... again.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260522-2-io.r9iRN5&refcode=em20260522-37808&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=37808%2E1203867%2EXCKgoi ]Tweet from @RepNancyMace: 'Ilhan Omar. Shri Thanedar. Pramila Jayapal.
All born in foreign countries, none were citizens by birth. All sitting in
United States Congress. All making clear every single day their loyalty is
not to America. We just introduced a long overdue joint resolution
proposing a constitutional amendment to require Members of Congress,
federal judges, and Senate-confirmed officers to be natural born citizens.
This is the very same standard the President and Vice President are
already required to meet. The people writing America's laws, confirming
America's judges, and representing America on the world stage should have
one loyalty: America. Not any other country. For too long we have allowed
foreign born members to hold seats in this government while making clear
they are America last, not America first. We see it every day. This
constitutional amendment will put an end to it.

Peter,
Nancy Mace wants us to be silent. She wants us to be afraid. She wants an
America for her, and for people who look like her. But that’s not what
this country is, and it never has been.

I’m a refugee, and I was given the opportunity for a new start in America.
I am eternally grateful for everything this country has given me. I ran
for Congress in the first place because I believe in America’s promise,
and I am never going to stop working to make sure we live up to that
promise.

I can stand against anything people like Nancy Mace and Donald Trump throw
my way because I have lived through things far worse than they can ever
imagine.

But I can’t do it alone.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260522-2-io.r9iRN5&refcode=em20260522-37808&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=37808%2E1203867%2EXCKgoi ]If you’re with me, and if I can count on you to stay by my side as we
fight for the nation we know the United States can be, please: split a
donation between Justice Democrats and my campaign for Congress today.

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

I want to be honest with you. In Washington, we’re surrounded by polls, charts, and reports telling us what voters are supposed to think heading into November. that required the government to put conservation on equal footing with oil and
gas interests. By repealing it, this administration has once again tipped the
scales further in favor of their Big Oil buddies. Bottom line, the Bureau of Land Management will no longer prioritize land
conservation. The move paves the way for wholesale drilling, mining, and logging
operations across millions of acres of public land. We can’t let that happen.To stop further destruction, we’re mobilizing grassroots opposition across the
country, and rallying environmental allies in Congress to block Trump’s
policies. But we need more support to keep this important work going, Peter — so, we’re asking: Can you renew your LCV membership for just $15 today? Republican Task Force Issue: 5/22/2026
Gabbard Out as DNI

Tulsi Gabbard [resigned Thursday](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LHOozAQBOCngc4IryHGhYtr6HLtlWixF7I6Y5BtQh7_V6I8wV-PNKNv_t2nO3LguP7FjWwqy-R3P5UzZF5xnjH5RJnXmDH7yNcELdxE2wuAKYZJ1t5651G6mqzU2nQGpDb1ww5Sk4KBnDPUSmVMOyg0pEAZMxuta7bvqrYHAAXQ66bXqjPyhosz3gwOq67FQKk0iY5zDuwwFsz_lz05aty-1cE-Sjlypf5UMFYwXtfVLPsr0pXfeQXjsQcu7HIFI71cODM_SXxs4osTX51Y0r6Jks7tEA5njlTqZP1xcQicb7rq2nVDDp_h8oufnhZ-AgAA__-cZnnA) as Director of National Intelligence (DNI), citing her husband's diagnosis with an extremely rare form of bone cancer as the reason for her departure. She steps down effective June 30. Gabbard led the intelligence community through the opening of the Iran war -- a critical test for any DNI. [Reuters confirmed](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFuhDAQRL_GdEawBxgXLtLQXdqUaLEXbhVjI9uEfH500Unp085Io3nv4z7fkT2H7R13Mqmss4tuLqfPvOGyYHKJMm8hY3aBrxkaGGTTS4A5-LmtnHHWYWsrMq1SutPQKl09zKBbGEfo3aDU2q2u0YijHvTYqYXWhSo2z6mmB4AbQK_qXt063Q64Wu30aFF0DXpKpU50nItni6Fg_lxjslTbuFfePEo5sri9CZgETNd11YnOQik_-2cSk3cCpjMLmF448sUjSzr3I8uAhWNALzkU8p43Cpak40S2xCTX-C0DXVk63rigl4mOmEqWfyIETFUy7rjYe86DEl2z7cj-92T5h9MvAz8BAAD___nXiFk) the resignation shortly after Fox News broke the exclusive. She was among Trump's most contested cabinet confirmations. Her exit leaves a critical post vacant as the Iran conflict remains unresolved. Thursday was a day of sweeping White House personnel shifts -- the administration also [swore in](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2OwyAQRk-DOyw8_iEUFNu4y7ZbWmMY2ygERwMJ1195j7DdJ33Se9L7uS93DDGk_RufZLlsiz_9Ut4xhx3XFdkz5bCnjNmnUBdQMEk1SoAlxaVrvPXOY-casp3WZjDQadMcFgxMblDdrXeEWiFo6iejaerB4GpuTbAXSo0A0AOMuh11P5huws0Zb24OxaAwEpeW6fVeY3CYCubHdrKj1p3PJtqjlFcW_ZeAWcBca23dmhPVfP0C5msKmB_0CUlW5HzIXE9OMiS5kSfGKJky8YekOzCwgLlh6181xBjypMWg9ieG-Ocr_8jzsfAbAAD___WrdVo) Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve Chair. ★★★
Warsh Takes the Fed

Kevin Warsh was [sworn in Thursday](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L1uhDAQBOCnMZ2RWX58FC7S0F3alGhtL7A640O2OV4_Io-QbqSRvpHm5zk_kQPH9Rt3Mqkss3_7uZwh84rWYvKJMq8xY_aRrxkUDFL1EmCOYW4qb7zz2LiKTKP12I3Q6LHajLYwwEL-0REMtm31w7a6d151BDRAU7G5KdUDQAvQ67rXbTc2Ay5u9OPDoegUBkqlTnScNrDDWDC_lndyVLv3XgWzlXJk0X4JmARM13XVLlp3lwKmmxcwqf7OIGAq6dwP-aIPR3lhyptcyEu3ISfJsVCiXGTCQrneyh6qZPxxcQicBy06te7I4W-4_OOnj4HfAAAA__8zhna-) as Federal Reserve Chair at the White House, replacing Jerome Powell. Trump publicly demanded lower interest rates at the ceremony, putting his expectations on record from the opening day. Markets are pricing the Fed on hold through most or all of 2026, as tariff-driven inflation complicates the rate-cut math. [What Trump wants](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0D2OrDAQBODTmAxkmv_AwUvI5qUboqbbQGuMGdmesfb2K_YIm5VU0ldSfT2WB4oTv__H05qQtoUvXtLbRdlxXTFwsFF2HzGyl7yAhr7UXQmweLfUBRsmxpoKa-phmNoJ6mEqDtOgRlpJa4v9SrjiCMh9O449gGXLhZib0h0ANADdUHVD0051jxtNPI2EqtXobEhVsK_36oTQJ4zP7QpkK7rOwpkjpVdUzT8Fs4I551yR93enYL51BbPu7gwKZkuXv85vBfPTfsSXGUM8ypiv4Evx5Wa5pAMlFMHwK4tzEvtBtXo_UdzvYPrDPx8DPwEAAP__cdZ0bQ) and what the economic data supports are already in conflict -- an unusual position for a new chair on day one. Warsh, a former Fed governor, takes the chair with monetary policy under unusual political pressure. [CBS News](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2OwyAQRk-DOyw8_iEUFNu4y7ZbWmMY2ygERwMJ1195j7DdJ33Se9L7uS93DDGk_RufZLlsiz_9Ut4xhx3XFdkz5bCnjNmnUBdQMEk1SoAlxaVrvPXOY-casp3WZjDQadMcFgxMblDdrXeEWiFo6iejaerB4GpuTbAXSo0A0AOMuh11P5huws0Zb24OxaAwEpeW6fVeY3CYCubHdrKj1p3PJtqjlFcW_ZeAWcBca23dmhPVfP0C5msKmB_0CUlW5HzIXE9OMiS5kSfGKJky8YekOzCwgLlh6181xBjypMWg9ieG-Ocr_8jzsfAbAAD___WrdVo) covered the White House ceremony as the formal handoff of an institution Trump has long sought to influence. ★★★
Rubio Rejects Hormuz Demand

Secretary of State Marco Rubio flatly rejected Iran's demand to establish a tolling system on the Strait of Hormuz as a condition for peace talks. [CBS News](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDuO5CAUAE-DMyx4_rAEBJs46003tJ7h2Y0agwW4keb0o54jTFxSqVT_H-sDffDx-IcnmVz31SW31jsUf-C2YXaZij9iweKibysImLmYOMAawyo7Z5x1KG1HRiqlRw1S6e5pJqH1tNlNCUKUg55pB2k1DWqw2u268-ajEhMADACT6ic1jFrOuFvt9B-LbBQYKNc-03VvwVuMFctrT9lSb9PZBfOs9Sps-MtgYbC01nq7lUitfDiDJfg38ftyWKkwWHzGyBtmXvN9Xvwu_CK0xCuGV-GlZvSVp50_Uz7vL25TrDkFBkuXjbuaD8GXWbFRHCf68NNQf7HsbeA7AAD__4DifdY) reported Rubio called the proposal "absolutely not acceptable." Iran says it is still reviewing the latest U.S. peace proposal. [NBC News reported](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOpDAQRL_GZB7hNtgQOLiEbC69EDV2w1hjDGqb4_dXs9ov2KikKqn09P495yfGFPP2F3dyXNc5HGGuVypxw2VBDkwlbrlgCTneM7RgZNtLgDmnWTXBBR9Q-YacsnbsRlB2bF5O4aAMGRP0MlgyqwGv205ZT570YtYmus9V2wOABujto7e6G5XB1Y9hHDyKrsVEXB9M57Wk6DFXLO_1YE8Pf-xNcq9azyL0HwGTgCkvPtNdPpuA6T44BQFTZMw_Ia8iK6Z3kZWv_ZSVXp92w7PIfPlEyDIQJnniO5aKWd7Ikn1G3Rnoh4ZdOO-YUizGiq7ddozpG6X-wtx_B18BAAD__3c7fzk) both sides acknowledge narrowed gaps but that fundamental disagreements remain -- over nuclear terms, regional influence, and control of key waterways. Trump said he would wait "a couple of days" for Tehran's response. [Reuters noted](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGunTAQRL_GdL4yewE_Fy7S0L20KdFiL7CKMchrLr8fkSIfkHJmpNHR-fU9fSMnzutP3MmXukzxiFO9kvCK84wlFhJes6DEzPcEBgZteg0w5TS1TfQxRGxDQ7611nUOWuuazdPShy8TBucsdb19ojGLjd3b2jkQNuyfK9MDwBugt6_evjvXDrgEF91XQNUZTFTqq9B5zYkD5oryezlKoFc49ib5rdZT1PuHglHBeN_3q9BVqcizP81RUlQwojDqEwMvHBSMlbaCWRf6MN2cV52wklR9iS4k55GFdC3Xfmq51pWkit5IB8z6Rq76n4JWwdgUH8-bU2IZrOrMuiOnv3j1P2x-PPwJAAD__xv1hhs) Iran is still weighing its reply as both sides continue indirect talks through intermediaries, with no timeline for a formal agreement.

Paxton vs. Cornyn: Four Days Out

With four days until the May 26 runoff, Trump's Paxton endorsement puts every Senate Republican on notice. If Paxton [upsets Cornyn](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDGOpDAQAF8DWSMwMB4HDi6ZbC-9ELXtBlprbOQ2x87vT3tP2KyiUqn-fCwfyJHT9hsPsqWuS8hhqVcU3tA5LKGQ8JYEJSS-F9WrB_QzKLWkuAxtsMEHHHxLdtDaTEYN2rS71RM5HcxAz9Eb7014hMnNfnSznvA5qpbtt6qflVKjUrPuZj1OZnjg6k0wT4_N1GOkUrtC5-Uie0wV5XPNxVPn89FGu9d6SjP-atSrUa_7vrvTSZfL1qhXolv2fJVGvc4cubKXb8SvmhMc-EkCOwusnDDCydXvwAnqTlDpCwWEElaCgp4AN-QkFXwu6Z3AXflNAdwbarmOU4BSyEXooFTbYsN5c4wsD91M_XYgx_-59Qd3_1r1LwAA__-aH46m), the establishment lane in 2026 primaries gets a lot narrower.

Both chambers left for Memorial Day recess without any immigration enforcement funding.

House Republican leaders [pulled a floor vote](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DGP4yAUBOBfgzsieNgQCopr3OXaK63nB3HQYbAAx39_lW22326kkT6N5t9jeWBMMW9_cQ-u9ufii1_6mVrccF2x-hpa3HLD5nO8FhCguZg4wJLTIgfvPHmUNAQnjbGjBWns8HLWktXGGqlWBd6uQvu7klL6AEJPIIboPpSYAEABTOY2GTVaqfFJ1ts7IRsFplD7rYbjXFMkzB3b_2epFG5U9iG5V-9HY-oPg5nBnFfK4WqfjsF8lBR7pMZgppK3GtonvsrZAv8RGyfMFBJ_lx74hZUf5Qq18V7P_eCxYuaVMqpRj_o-VOePK6YUmzZsFNuOMX1v6b-47u3gKwAA__8prH8r) on a Senate war powers resolution after Democrats, with Republican defectors, had enough votes to pass it — averting a bipartisan rebuke of Trump's Iran war authority.

body:
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
A Letter from Alex
On May 7th we began our By The People Tour with our first event held in Grand Junction. This Tour is not your typical political event. It is a series of workshops across the district where neighbors come together, build community and have a role and voice in writing the plan that we want for our future.
We’re the people who pay the bills, build daring things for Colorado, show up for our neighbors, and keep our communities running. And nobody knows what our communities and our families need better than us. But nobody in Congress ever bothers to ask. When lobbyists, corporate donors, and consultants set the menu, we’re not just excluded — we’re on that menu.
That’s why I’m traveling across Colorado’s 3rd District to hear directly from the people who live and work here. I moderate a discussion by asking a few simple questions: What do people love about where they live? What have they lost under Jeff Hurd and Donald Trump? What needs to be restored? What do people want Congress to do for us when we take back the House and Senate in November?
Since launching, we have held 8 events in total and have another 12 scheduled or in the works. I am happy and heartened to say that we have received overwhelming feedback and support. This is how we win in November and defeat Jeff Hurd: by showing up, engaging with people, listening and learning from them, and developing our plan with them for when I get to Congress. It’s exciting and people are excited!
If you are near one of our events (see the end of this newsletter for a calendar), I invite you to join. And if you are not, you can visit our website [https://alexkelloff.com/by-the-people-tour] or Facebook page ( @alexkelloffco [https://www.facebook.com/alexkelloffco/] ) and fill out a survey to help build the plan.
After completing our By The People Tour in mid-June, we will compile the results and produce the “By The People Plan!” We are looking forward to continuing this hard work, listening to and learning from you, and producing the plan over the next 4 weeks!
See you out there on our By The People Tour!
— Alex
May Recap
May has been another strong month for our campaign as we continue building momentum across Colorado’s 3rd District. We officially kicked off our “By the People” tour, a campaign rooted in listening to communities across the district and building around their priorities.
The tour began in Grand Junction where Alex was joined by leaders in the public lands and conservation space to discuss the future of Colorado’s public lands, water, and outdoor economy. Protecting our public lands continues to be one of the issues voters raise most often across the district, and Alex remains committed to taking those priorities to Washington.
On May 9th, Alex volunteered in Pitkin County helping pick up trash as part of a local community cleanup effort before attending Dandelion Day. In Carbondale, Alex made the second “By the People” stop and had meaningful conversations and strong engagement with community members from across the Roaring Fork Valley.
Throughout the month, Alex continued traveling across the district with visits to Pagosa Springs, Durango, Dolores, and Ridgway, meeting with residents, local leaders, and community advocates to hear directly about the challenges facing Western and Southern Colorado. The final stops of May will include Montrose, Glenwood Springs, and Meeker.
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
This month also included important conversations focused on housing, workforce development, and organized labor. Alex met with Executive Director Emilee Powell and Deputy Director Jason Colunga at Housing Resources of Western Colorado to discuss housing affordability and community needs across the region. He also met with Jason Carrico, Business Manager of United Association of Plumbers & Pipefitters Local 145, and toured their Pipe Trades Educational Center to learn more about workforce training, apprenticeship programs, and the importance of investing in skilled labor and infrastructure.
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]We are also proud to announce that Alex earned the endorsement of Voces Unidas de las Montañas.
In their endorsement, they shared:
“We are endorsing you because you have taken the time to listen, build relationships and show commitment to rural Latino communities across the Western Slope. You have made yourself accessible, sought our advice and demonstrated responsiveness and growth in your understanding of our priorities.”
This endorsement reflects what this campaign is about: showing up, listening, building relationships, and earning trust through action and engagement.
As we continue through the summer, our mission remains the same. We are meeting people where they are, listening to their concerns, and building a campaign By the People and for the people of Colorado’s 3rd District.
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
Holding Hurd Accountable
Funding Insurrectionists on Your Dime: Jeff Hurd’s total compliance with Washington insiders reached a new low this month following the Justice Department’s creation of a $1.776 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund.” Rolled out on May 18, 2026, as part of a highly unorthodox settlement for a personal civil lawsuit, this massive pool of taxpayer money is being pulled directly from the federal Judgment Fund to provide payouts to political allies and individuals charged in the January 6th Capitol riots.
The fund is explicitly designed to bypass standard judicial review, leaving a hand-picked, five-member commission with the unchecked power to privately distribute large sums of public money to party loyalists. What makes this arrangement completely unacceptable is the timing. Hurd is keeping quiet on this unprecedented corrupt payout while simultaneously supporting budget measures that gut Medicaid, SNAP, housing, and education programs across Western and Southern Colorado.
Instead of fighting to keep our hard-earned tax dollars in our communities to support local hospitals and schools, Hurd is allowing those resources to be carved up as a rewards system for the well-connected. Colorado deserves a representative who protects our district’s economic wellbeing rather than standing by while the federal government bankrolls an ongoing giveaway to an inner circle.
What’s Coming Soon
We will continue with our By the People tour and have a few more stops. We are looking forward to visiting the various communities across the district and engaging in conversations with you all. Hope to see you there!
* May 22nd — Montrose from 10am-12pm at Montrose Police Dept. Community Room
* May 26th — Glenwood Springs from 5-7pm at Glenwood Springs Community Center
* May 27th — Meeker from 5-6:30pm at Mountain Valley Bank
* June 4th — Paonia/Hotchkiss from 5:30-7pm at Big B’s
* June 8th — Trinidad from 4:30-6:30pm at Trinidad Community Center Meeting Room
* June 9th — Alamosa from 5-7pm at The Barn at Manzanilla Farm
* June 11th — Gunnison from 5:30-7pm at Gunnison Library
* June 14th - Grand Junction from 10am-12pm at Mesa County Democrats Office
You’ll also be hearing Alex’s voice on the airwaves. Throughout May, Alex joined several podcasts and radio shows to talk about the race and the issues that matter most to Southern and Western Colorado. Alex was on the Peanut Butter and Mountains podcast, Pagosa Daily Post, the KDNK radio show, and the Yellow Scene Magazine.
If you’d like to add a By the People stop and meet with Alex, ask questions, and share your thoughts, please email campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] and a member of our team will follow up quickly to discuss scheduling. We’d also be happy to schedule a virtual meet and greet.
We’d love to hear from you — it’s incredibly important that Alex hears from the people he hopes to represent.
What You Can Do
1. FOLLOW ON SOCIAL MEDIA: Stay up to date with my team at Facebook [https://www.facebook.com/alexkelloffco/] , X [https://x.com/alexkelloffco] , Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/alexkelloffco/] , TikTok [https://www.tiktok.com/@alexkelloffco] , Bluesky [https://bsky.app/profile/alexkelloffco.bsky.social] and Substack [https://substack.com/@alexkelloffco?]

2. VOLUNTEER: Sign up to get involved with my campaign » [https://alexkelloff.com/volunteer]

3. FINANCIALLY SUPPORT: Donate to my campaign today » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak]

4. HOST A MEET & GREET: Contact campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] , and we’ll quickly follow up with you to discuss hosting an event.

5. INTRODUCE ALEX TO VOTERS IN THE DISTRICT: Contact field@alexkelloff.com [field@alexkelloff.com] for more details.
